summary.headline: Gateway Distriparks guides rail volumes to a 100,000 TEU/quarter floor and expects double-digit growth next year, with Q2 realisation up ~5% YoY.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as a sequential recovery from a weak Q1, with rail volumes up about 11% QoQ and container-business EBITDA back to the roughly INR 100 crore per quarter run-rate seen before the war-driven disruption. Realisation rose about 5% YoY and 7% QoQ, mainly from fuel-linked price pass-throughs and mix, with Ankleshwar EXIM expected to dilute realisation per TEU. Snowman Logistics' warehousing and transport lines are improving, but PAT remains thin because of interest and depreciation from ongoing reinvestment. Management also addressed the Western DFC connection to JNPT, the Jaipur ICD court case, and the Indore ICD timeline.

segments.name: Container business (GDL standalone + Kerala + Kashipur, CFS, ICD, rail, road)
segments.commentary: Rail volume recovered ~11% QoQ; management targets at least 100,000 TEU per quarter. Realisation per TEU expected to fall as Ankleshwar EXIM ramps on shorter lead distance.

segments.name: Snowman Logistics - Warehousing
segments.commentary: Pallets stored up ~10% YoY; warehousing revenue grew ~10-11%. Warehousing margin percentage has fallen, which management attributes to park-and-pay (under 10% margin), build-to-suit, 5PL mix and wage/power cost pass-through lags.

segments.name: Snowman Logistics - 5PL
segments.commentary: Segment grew only 1-2% YoY; no new customers added in FY27 so far. One major customer expanded scope to pan-India.

segments.name: Snowman Logistics - Transport and PAT
segments.commentary: Revenue slightly lower as 5PL growth lagged; PAT remains negligible due to higher interest and depreciation from reinvestment.

guidance_outlook: Rail volumes: 100,000 TEU per quarter is the bare minimum for the rest of FY27; full-year double-digit growth is uncertain given the weak Q1.
FY28: management maintains double-digit rail volume growth, aided by a full year of Ankleshwar EXIM operations.
Snowman: expects to cross INR 100 crore EBITDA in FY27; 5PL to catch up in Q3 and Q4 to meet targets.
Indore ICD: civil and rail works underway; targeting operations by December 2027, with about 6 months to start contributing volumes and about 2 years to ramp up.
Jaipur ICD: final arguments done and order reserved; operations could start up to 18 months after a favourable order.
New projects are underwritten at a minimum 15% IRR and 7-year payback.
capex_capacity: Snowman: about 23,000 pallets under construction for delivery in the next few months, with a further ~20,000 pallets under discussion.
Snowman: new facilities are fully cold/temperature-controlled; dry is about 10-12% of existing capacity.
Snowman: some park-and-pay leases ended, reducing reported pallet capacity QoQ.
Gateway: Indore ICD civil and rail works in full swing; Ankleshwar MMLP has received all EXIM permissions, with B/L points being opened and volumes still minimal.
Capex mix includes replacing leased trains with owned trains and fleet electrification.
demand_pricing: Price increases were implemented after fuel hikes and passed through to customers, with matching cost increases.

Western DFC: Gateway ran the first double-stack train on JNPT on 20 June; JNPT rail share is only 14-15%. Management estimates 10,000-15,000 TEU per month move by road to the north that could shift to DFC rail, but shipping-line routing decisions are the main driver and remain unclear.
Indian Railways tariff rationalisation for JNPT has been requested by the industry; management says it is too early to quantify any pass-through.
Market share: management says it has held share in NCR, Punjab and Uttarakhand against bundled offerings from Adani and CONCOR, citing terminal network and IT (EDI, tracking, OCR).
Snowman: power cost increases of 6-8% are built into annual contracts; wage hikes (Karnataka ~70%, Haryana ~35%) and gratuity/PF changes not yet passed through.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for rail volume momentum over the next half and year, given macro weakness?
qa_highlights.answer: Samvid Gupta expects a similar trend; 100,000 TEU per quarter is the minimum target. Domestic volumes have started and Ankleshwar EXIM adds volume from Q3. Double-digit growth is maintained for next year, though this year is uncertain after Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ~5% YoY realisation gain structural or mix-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly a pass-through of fuel-linked price increases, with cost increases matching. Ankleshwar mix lowers realisation per TEU because of shorter lead distance, so management will focus on EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: What is Snowman's profit prospect, and can it reach INR 10-15 crore quarterly PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is reinvesting, so interest and depreciation stay high. It highlights operating cash flow and EBITDA growth, and says PAT growth is possible but not the focus. 5PL is being grown selectively because of low margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and timeline of the Jaipur ICD court case?
qa_highlights.answer: Final arguments are complete and the order is reserved. If the order is favourable, operations could start within 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: How much EBITDA upside can DFC bring beyond volume, and when will it show?
qa_highlights.answer: Hard to predict because other operators also benefit. Turnaround time and asset utilisation will improve, but volume depends on shipping lines, which have not indicated any change in JNPT calls.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Snowman warehousing margin percentage declined over the long term?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites park-and-pay (margins under 10%), build-to-suit at lower margins, 5PL mix, cost reclassification and unpassed wage and power costs. Core owned and long-term-lease cold storage margins are said to be intact.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex return threshold and asset turnover outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Asset turnover is hard to give because capex includes replacement, train ownership shift and electrification. New projects target at least 15% IRR and a 7-year payback.

risks_watch: Shipping lines' JNPT calling decisions drive DFC benefit; no indication yet from lines.
Weak Q1 means full-year rail volume growth may fall short of double digits.
Snowman warehousing margin pressure from wage/gratuity/PF changes not yet passed through on annual contracts.
Snowman utilisation at about 85% versus 88-89% target; park-and-pay exposure is volatile.
Jaipur ICD court order timing; Indore ICD commissioning slipping past December 2027 would delay revenue.
Macro uncertainty: the war and tariff situation are cited as unresolved.
summary.management_tone: Confident on rail volume recovery and the DFC opportunity, but cautious and non-committal on the timing of JNPT volume shifts and full-year growth. Defensive on Snowman's low PAT and declining warehousing margin percentage, which management attributes to mix, reinvestment and cost pass-through lags.
